reason: Reports colour, oxidation parameters and α-tocopherol of olive oil after deep frying three products, contrasting oil without and with previous heating at 170 °C for 10 h.
foods: Arbequina extra virgin olive oil (frying medium)
treatments: Raw oil vs heated oil (170 °C for 10 h, cooled 10 h), each then used at 170 °C to deep fry French fries (5 min) or Iberian pork sirloin from indoor or outdoor pigs (3 min)
methods_quote: Raw or heated oil (1050 mL) was placed in a fryer and heated at 170 °C. The basket with the products (no overlapping) was then put inside the fryer, which was kept uncapped. After frying, the basket was left to drain over the fryer for 2 min.
units: colour coordinates (unitless); PV mEq O2 kg−1; α-tocopherol mg kg−1; P values
replicates: Four replicates were performed per oil type (raw and heated) and per product (French fries and sirloin from the two types of pork).

reason: Reports frying losses (a direct deep-frying effect) and properties of French fries and pork sirloin fried in raw versus previously heated olive oil.
foods: French fries (potato); Iberian pork sirloin from indoor and outdoor reared pigs
treatments: Deep frying at 170 °C in raw or previously heated (170 °C, 10 h) olive oil: French fries 5 min, sirloin medallions 3 min; drained 2 min
methods_quote: Raw or heated oil (1050 mL) was placed in a fryer and heated at 170 °C. The basket with the products (no overlapping) was then put inside the fryer, which was kept uncapped. After frying, the basket was left to drain over the fryer for 2 min.
retention_quote: The frying losses were calculated by weighing the samples immediately before and after frying.
units: colour (unitless); frying losses %; fat, moisture, MDA mg kg−1; shear force kg; work of shear kg s−1; P values
replicates: Four replicates were performed per oil type (raw and heated) and per product (French fries and sirloin from the two types of pork).
